quiz.q: Why did Gandhi distinguish Satyagraha from passive resistance?
options: Satyagraha treats non-violence as an article of faith rather than a tactical choice born of weakness.
Satyagraha permits the strategic use of physical force whenever political negotiations completely break down.
Passive resistance requires unconditional love and self-suffering to convert the heart of the opponent.
Passive resistance seeks to destroy the wrongdoer, whereas Satyagraha aims only to defeat state laws.
quiz.why: Gandhi maintained that while passive resistance avoids violence out of weakness, Satyagraha adopts non-violence as a moral principle and harbors no ill will toward the opponent.

quiz.q: According to Gandhi's model of oceanic circles of power, how should political Swaraj function?
options: Power should be concentrated in a centralized parliamentary state to ensure rapid modern development.
Power expands outward from self-controlled individuals to empower decentralized, self-reliant village republics.
Power must be transferred directly from colonial administrators to an educated national elite class.
Power resides exclusively in armed local militias organized to resist foreign political intervention.
quiz.why: Gandhi rejected top-down elite rule, proposing oceanic circles where authority radiates outward from self-disciplined individuals to autonomous village republics.

quiz.q: How does Gandhi's doctrine of trusteeship address the relationship between capital and labour?
options: By demanding state ownership of factories to eliminate all private business enterprise.
By urging workers to wage class struggle until capitalist owners are dispossessed.
By encouraging owners to consider wealth a community trust and serve society.
By adopting rapid mechanization to eliminate manual labour and maximize factory wages.
quiz.why: Gandhi rejected Marxist class conflict, advocating class harmony where capitalists act as moral trustees rather than sole owners of socially produced wealth.

quiz.q: Why did Gandhi characterize modern Western civilisation as 'satanic' in Hind Swaraj?
options: It relies on foreign religious doctrines rather than traditional Western philosophical teachings.
It rejects technological progress and prevents nations from expanding industrial manufacturing capacity.
It prioritizes colonial military alliances over diplomatic negotiations with non-Western sovereign territories.
It reduces humans to desire-driven creatures by endlessly multiplying material wants and consumer appetites.
quiz.why: Gandhi criticized modern civilisation for its relentless consumerism and materialism, arguing that true civilisation lies in self-restraint and minimizing wants.
